title: The Hitchhiker's Guide to Agentic AI
hook: A practitioner reference that walks the whole agent stack — transformer substrate, RLHF, memory, MCP, A2A, multi-agent topologies — on the thesis that good agents demand understanding every layer.
key_points: A comprehensive practitioner's reference for building autonomous AI systems, first principles to production.
Central thesis: great agentic systems require understanding every layer of the pipeline, not just one.
Foundations: transformers, GPU systems, SFT/LoRA/MoE, model compression, inference optimization.
Alignment & reasoning: RLHF, PPO, DPO, GRPO, reward modeling, chain-of-thought, test-time scaling.
Agentic core: trajectory RL, RAG and Agentic RAG, memory systems, harness/context design, MCP, A2A, and multi-agent topologies.
content_html: The Hitchhiker's Guide to Agentic AI is a practitioner's reference for building autonomous AI systems end to end — and a useful map if you're trying to see how the pieces fit together rather than studying one in isolation.
extra_html:
What it covers

The book is organized around a single thesis: building great agentic systems means understanding every layer of the pipeline. It starts with the LLM substrate — transformer architecture, GPU systems, training and fine-tuning (SFT, LoRA, MoE), model compression, and inference optimization — treated as foundations rather than the focus. It then builds the alignment and reasoning layer: RLHF, PPO, DPO and variants, GRPO, reward modeling, and RL for reasoning models including chain-of-thought and test-time scaling.

The second half is agentic AI proper: trajectory-based RL, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG and Agentic RAG), memory systems (in-context, external, episodic, semantic), agent harness and context management, and a taxonomy of design patterns. Inter-agent coordination gets real depth — the Model Context Protocol (MCP), agent skills and tool use, the Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocol, and centralized, decentralized, and hierarchical multi-agent topologies — closing with frameworks, agentic UI, evaluation, and deployment. Each chapter pairs theory with code and pointers to the primary literature; it's linked as the source for anyone who wants the full treatment.

related.title: Agentic Environment Engineering: A Survey
related.hook: Agents only get as good as the worlds they practice in. This survey maps the full lifecycle of agent environments — how we model, synthesize, evaluate, and grow them.

related.title: Model Context Protocol (MCP): A Standard for Connecting LLMs to Tools
related.hook: MCP is an open protocol that standardizes how AI applications expose tools, data, and resources to models - think USB-C for AI tool integrations.

related.title: Agent2Agent (A2A) Protocol
related.hook: A2A is an open standard for agents from different vendors to discover and delegate to each other — the agent-to-agent complement to MCP's agent-to-tool layer.
